audit.report: A replayable inventory reconciliation batch worker (pid 118867) held an idle transaction open for 4.0 seconds and blocked 12 checkout sessions, degrading checkout from 53% success over 15 seconds to 27% over 30 seconds against a 95% SLO. With $13,493 per minute at risk and a business tolerance of only 60 seconds of degradation, waiting for the batch's remaining ~896 seconds would have cost roughly $201,500. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the batch, the Continuity Guardian accepted because the workload is idempotent, checkpoint-resumable, replayable in about 4 minutes, and no protected settlements were in flight, and the Authority authorized the action in one round. The executor terminated pid 118867 and the verifier confirmed recovery: 36/36 checkouts succeeded over 10 seconds (100%), no lock waits remain, and no protected settlement was aborted. The business is back.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory workload left an idle transaction open, creating a lock chain that blocked checkout sessions and drove success below SLO.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory (inventory_reconcile), monitor for idle-in-transaction state and auto-terminate after a short threshold because it is idempotent, checkpoint-resumable, and replayable in ~4 minutes, making termination far cheaper than waiting during checkout degradation.

Pre-stage the replay cost (4 min) and typical runtime (900s) for batch_replayable_inventory in runbooks so the next negotiation can compute waiting cost versus replay cost in seconds instead of minutes.
audit.negotiation_critique: The guardians reasoned correctly in one round: the Database Guardian cited lock, telemetry, and business evidence, and the Continuity Guardian accepted with no objection because all invariants were satisfied. No round was wasted, no evidence was missed, and no invariant overrode the decision.
follow_ups: Ask the inventory-platform team why batch_replayable_inventory (pid 118867) stayed idle in transaction for 4.0 seconds and add an alert for idle-in-transaction duration on that application.
Confirm inventory_reconcile resumed from its last checkpoint after the 4-minute replay and validate that no inventory records were left partially reconciled.
Update the checkout runbook with the computed waiting cost (~$201,500) versus replay cost (4 minutes) for this workload so future incidents can be decided faster.
